body:
Triage: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:engine`, Task, M — this is restoration of a ruled axis, not a new convention decision: ADR-0053 D-A3 already declares the matrix as `driver × {SQLite, Postgres at minimum}`, and today that declared axis is enforced by nothing the census can see, which is exactly how #11456 sat green while PG threw 42883. Scope: give `check:driver-conformance` the dialect axis, with the deliberate-vs-accidental distinction carried by an explicit marker — the existing `dialectCell('sqlite')` call is the candidate the card names (7 files already use it); an unmarked hard-coded client in a conformance-named suite becomes a named finding. First measurement of the 99-literal population lands as a one-act baseline in the #5480 `$comment` discipline (not newly written looseness, not a raised ratchet), maintainer-vetoable at review. ⛔ Do not reclassify the 99 by guesswork — the gate only needs to force the *marking*, not to decide each file's intent for it.

Clause-②: **no** — a census/gate script plus a convention marker. No public surface widens and no accept/reject door on a shipped contract moves.

## ⚠️ Re-measured at claim, and the numbers have moved — in the direction that strengthens the card

The card measured `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src` a day ago. Measured again just now on `origin/main`:

| | card | now | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| files with a literal `client: 'better-sqlite3'` | 99 | **105** | +6 |
| files routing through `live-dialect-matrix` | 40 | **44** | +4 |
| files using `dialectCell(` | 7 | **7** | **0** |

⇒ the invisible population grows with ordinary work while the marker that would make it visible stays flat. This is not a static debt to pay down once; it accretes, which is the argument for closing it at the **census** rather than by sweeping files.

## Serial constraints cleared

Primary surface `scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs` and `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts` — no open PR touches either (checked across all open PRs).

⛔ Two test files **are** held by in-flight work and must not be edited:
- `sql-driver-11224-update-stamp-precision.test.ts` — #11572 / PR #12112, enqueued.
- `sql-driver-11794-richtext-text-family.test.ts` — #11875 / PR #12119, in flight.

⛔ `sql-driver.ts` bands `8600–9200` (#12015), `10100–10560` (#11722) and `13275–13900` (#11875) are all held. This card should need none of them.

## What is ruled and what is yours

Triage queued this without prescribing a fix, and the card is explicit that closing it *"means deciding what marks a deliberate single-cell suite … a convention decision, not a mechanical edit"*. `dialectCell('sqlite')` already exists for exactly that purpose and 7 files use it **alongside** the literal, so the marker is not hypothetical.

⛔ **The 105 are not 105 defects** and must never be reported as such — `sql-driver-11321-sqlite-audit-default-canonical.test.ts` is about SQLite *by name*. The gap is that "deliberately single-dialect" and "accidentally single-dialect" are **spelled identically today**.

**Bounded shape**: give the census a dialect axis so the number becomes visible and honest, with `dialectCell()` as the marker of deliberateness. **Report the classification counts; do not reclassify all 105 files** — that is a sweep, and it is a separate card whose size this one's number should decide.

The instance that proves the cost is measured and in-repo: #11456 sat green on `main` and on every PR while, on live PG 16.13, `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max` over a boolean column threw SQLSTATE `42883`.

**ACCEPT** — PR #12134. And both open questions are answered below; neither needs the maintainer.

### The ablation reproduces the defect instead of arguing it

This is the part that makes the card closable. The baseline census was run on the clean tree **and** on a tree where `sql-driver-aggregation-conformance.test.ts`'s testkit import was broken — reproducing the pre-#11456 state at the level the census reads:

> baseline census exit 0, `45 covered cell(s)` on **BOTH** trees — `diff` of the two runs is **EMPTY**

That empty diff *is* #12014, demonstrated rather than described. The new gate then exits 1 with `DIALECTED errors: 1`, naming the file. A gate card's ablation has to show the gate catching the thing the old one couldn't, on the same tree, and this does.

### The population design is better than what I sketched at dispatch

I framed the marker as `dialectCell()`. The dev inverted it: **the population is defined by the presence of a stance DECLARATION, not the absence of a `client` literal.** That matters — under my framing, moving a driver config into a helper would respell a suite out of the gate's reach silently. Under this one it cannot.

Scoring is **per file, not per cell**, with the reason stated: `FILTER_TEXT_CASES` is covered by both a matrix suite and an undeclared one, and per-cell scoring would let the undeclared one hide behind its neighbour. That is the right call and it is the kind of thing that is only visible if you actually run the census.

### My fences held, and the 105 were not treated as defects

- **One file changed** — `scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs`. **Zero `*.test.ts` edits**, verified. That was the fence that mattered most, and it kept the PR minimal.
- The gate scores **7 test files** (5 matrix, 2 undeclared) plus 1 non-test covering file — not 105. ⛔ The "105 are not 105 defects" instruction was honoured literally.
- The 2 undeclared suites went into a `DIALECT_LEDGER` as a **measured baseline rather than marked**, with the reason: *"marking them would record a claim about intent I cannot verify"*. That is exactly the line I drew, held without being asked twice.

**Independent corroboration**: the dev re-measured the population on `origin/main` at `e7480a8067` and got **105 / 44 / 7** — my numbers exactly, from a separate measurement.

One more piece of discipline worth naming: mid-branch the dev replaced its own hand-rolled `stripComments` with `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, the repo's single answer to "comment or code", and **verified the census output was byte-identical across the swap** — *"a change of provenance and not of measurement"* — then re-ran the ablation from scratch because the detector had changed.

---

## Answering both open questions — PM rulings, measured not argued

### Q1 — the two ledgered suites: **option A**, as a follow-up card

I measured both halves rather than taking the recommendation:

| claim | measurement on `origin/main` |
|---|---|
| `icontains` is already matrix-covered by another suite | `sql-driver-text-case-conformance.test.ts` mentions `icontains` **16 times**, and routes through the testkit ✅ |
| the comparand-type case-set claims universality it does not measure | `check-driver-conformance.mjs:231`, verbatim: *"the comparand-type door: the six accepted types **compile everywhere**, everything else is refused loudly — #7872"* ✅ |

⇒ **A is right, and the dev's concession toward B is unnecessary.** `icontains` genuinely is covered on all three dialects by its neighbour, so `sql-driver-icontains-and-retired-operators.test.ts` is a second pass over covered ground and marking it `dialectCell('sqlite')` loses nothing. B would convert a suite that adds **no** dialect coverage.

The comparand-type conversion is the one that is *earned*: it is the only dialect-scored cell with no matrix-routed suite at all, against a case-set whose own prose claims the accepted types compile **everywhere**.
